metaDescription: Six Roborock robot vacuums from the Q7 L5 to the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro, compared on suction labels, docks, edge mopping, slim bodies and upkeep.
expertTake: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is the top pick because it balances 20,000 Pa, a FlexiArm edge mop and a zero-tangle brush pair at a sane price tier. The Q7 L5 is the value pick, a laser robot without a dock. Anyone with a small, tidy flat should skip the Qrevo line and buy a Q-series.
introParagraphs: This brand sells in two clear families. The Q-series covers laser-guided robots with a bag dock or no dock at all, and the Qrevo and Saros ranges add wash stations, extending mops and obstacle sensing. The names read like a code, which is the main hurdle.

The practical differences are physical: does the dock wash pads, does the mop reach corners, how tall is the body and how well does it climb. This guide sorts six models by those mechanisms and names the compromise each one makes.

products.name: Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro, 20,000 Pa, FlexiArm edge mop, dual zero-tangle
products.description:
The Qrevo 2 Pro is built to solve three complaints at once. Its FlexiArm edge mop swings outward to reach corners and baseboards, a dual zero-tangle system keeps long hair from wrapping brushes, and the dock empties, washes and dries without your help. A 20,000 Pa rating sits behind that for rugs.

It sits one step above the Qrevo S5V on suction, 20,000 Pa against 12,000 Pa, and below the Edge 3 Pro on price. The suction figure is a peak, so the reason to buy it is the combination of edge reach and hair handling, which does more for daily cleaning than the headline number. If you want one robot for a family home with a dog, this is the balanced choice. Owners with a mixed hardwood and rug layout should still mark the thickest rugs as no-mop zones in the app.

The upkeep is dock upkeep. Wipe the wash tray weekly, rinse the dirty-water tank after each mop run and descale the water path every few months. Replace mop pads and bags on schedule, and trim the brushes if strands escape the zero-tangle system.
products.bestFor: Family homes with pets that want edge mopping and a full dock.
pros: FlexiArm mop reaches baseboards and corners
cons: Pads and bags are ongoing parts

products.name: Roborock Qrevo Edge 3 Pro, 36,000 Pa, 300+ objects, 3.46 in body
products.description:
The Edge 3 Pro leans on mechanical agility more than the other Roborocks. Its retractable laser scanner gives 360 degree mapping while keeping the body at 3.46 in, and the listing says it glides over thresholds and uneven floors. A recognition system names over 300 types of obstacle, which implies a camera or similar sensor.

It is the top tier of the range, with a 36,000 Pa rating that is the highest here and a price to match. Against the Saros 10R it is slightly taller, 3.46 in against 3.14 in, but clears more thresholds. A home with uneven floors, rugs and pets gets the most from it. Compared with the Qrevo 2 Pro it buys climbing and recognition, not edge reach, so decide which problem is yours.

The moving parts need care. Keep the retractable scanner free of lint, wipe the wash tray and empty the tanks. Because the recognition suggests a camera, check the privacy settings in the app before you start the first run. The thresholds are the quiet selling point, since a robot that stalls on a doorway track never finishes the rest of the house.
products.bestFor: Homes with thresholds, rugs and pets that want recognition.
pros: 36,000 Pa label is the highest here
Retractable scanner keeps the body low
Glides over thresholds and uneven floors
cons: Top price tier of the range
More moving parts to keep clean

products.name: Roborock Saros 10R, 22,000 Pa, 3.14 in slim, StarSight 2.0
products.description:
The Saros 10R is the slim flagship. At 3.14 in it reaches under furniture that blocks the Edge 3 Pro, and the StarSight Autonomous System 2.0 uses 3D sensing to navigate and avoid obstacles. A zero-tangle brush and edge-cleaning design handle hair and baseboards.

Its 22,000 Pa label is below the Edge 3 Pro and above the Qrevo 2 Pro, and its edge is the combination of low height with real sensing. It costs less than the Edge 3 Pro, so it suits buyers whose furniture is the limiting factor. The body is the story here, not the suction. Because a slim body has less room for a big bin, empty the dock bag on the early side in a shedding household.

Care matches the dock-based line: empty the tanks, wipe the wash area and keep the sensors clear. Keep the forward sensing window free of dust, because a slim body has little room to hide it. The slim shell also means less battery volume, so check the runtime on large floors before you commit.
products.bestFor: Homes with low sofas and beds that want a high-end Roborock.
cons: Less climbing ability than the Edge 3 Pro

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S5V, 12,000 Pa, FlexiArm mop, warm-air drying dock
products.description:
The Qrevo S5V is the middle of the dock range. A brushless HyperForce motor gives 12,000 Pa, FlexiArm edge mopping reaches corners and a dock with warm-air drying keeps pads from souring. Smart obstacle sensing and a dual zero-tangle system complete the package.

It matches the Qrevo 2 Pro on edge reach but has 12,000 Pa to the Pro's 20,000 Pa, and it costs less. For hard-floor homes the lower number makes no practical difference. It is the best-balanced entry to the wash-dock family. Owners moving up from a Q-series will notice the pad washing first, since the mop no longer needs rinsing by hand.

Expect the usual dock chores: empty the dirty tank, wipe the tray, replace bags and pads, and descale. Warm-air drying helps, but a dock left wet for days still develops a smell. Leaving the lid slightly open when the robot is away speeds the drying and cuts the smell further.
products.bestFor: Hard-floor homes that want a wash dock at a mid tier.
cons: 12,000 Pa is lower than the Pro models
Pads and bags are ongoing parts

products.name: Roborock LiDAR vacuum and mop, 10,000 Pa, 2.7 L bag, 7 to 9 weeks
products.description:
This Q-series variant is the plain bag-dock Roborock. LiDAR maps the home, the JawScrapers main brush is a comb that sheds hair and a 2.7 L sealed bag lasts up to 7 to 9 weeks. The listing highlights deep carpet and edge cleaning with 10,000 Pa.

It has no pad washing, so the mop is a hand-rinsed pad, which is the compromise that keeps the price in a lower tier than the Qrevo S5V. Against the Q7 L5 it adds a dock and 2,000 Pa. If you vacuum more than you mop, a bag dock is the sensible, low-maintenance middle. The pad can be removed and tossed in a washing machine in a net bag, which keeps the running cost low.

The routine is small: change the bag, rinse the mop pad, clear the main brush and wipe the cliff sensors. Because it shares parts with other Q-series models, spares are easy to find. Many owners keep a spare pair of side brushes in a drawer so a swap takes a minute.
products.bestFor: Vacuum-first homes that want a bag dock without a wash station.
pros: Sealed 2.7 L bag lasts 7 to 9 weeks
Lower tier than the Qrevo docks
cons: Mop pad is rinsed by hand

products.name: Roborock Q7 L5 vacuum and mop, 8,000 Pa, LiDAR, no dock
products.description:
The Q7 L5 is the entry laser robot of the range. A 360 degree laser maps rooms in real time, a specially shaped main brush and zero-tangle side brush deal with hair and an attached mop handles damp work. There is no dock beyond a charging base.

Its 8,000 Pa is the lowest figure in this guide, and it empties by hand, which is why it costs the least. Compared with the Roborock bag-dock model above it loses two weeks of convenience and 2,000 Pa. For a flat with hard floors it is plenty.

The routine is the shortest in the family: empty the bin, rinse the filter and mop cloth, trim the brush and wipe the laser window. There are no bags to buy, so the running cost is minimal. Remember that the laser needs a clear view, so move low chairs before the first mapping run so the outline of each room is clean.
products.bestFor: Flats and small homes that want a laser map for the least money.
pros: Laser mapping at the lowest tier
No bags or tanks to maintain

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Q-series covers laser robots with no dock or a bag dock. The Qrevo models add wash docks and FlexiArm mops, and the Saros models focus on slim bodies and sensing. Choose the family by dock need first, and then by height and suction. Most buyers who regret a purchase in this range bought a wash dock they never used, or skipped one they later wanted, so be honest about how often you mop.

A round robot misses the last inch of a corner. FlexiArm extends the mop on the Qrevo 2 Pro and S5V to touch baseboards. If your rooms are rectangular with long skirting, it matters more than extra suction.

The Saros 10R is 3.14 in tall, and the Edge 3 Pro is 3.46 in but glides over thresholds. Measure your sofa gap and your highest doorway track. Add a half inch of margin, because bumpers and thick rug edges add height. A robot that cannot cross a track is stuck in one room.
The Edge 3 Pro names over 300 object types and the Saros 10R uses 3D sensing. Recognition usually relies on a camera-style sensor. If you want no lens in the house, stay with the laser-only Q-series.

The Q7 L5 has a charge base, the bag-dock model empties itself, and the Qrevo models wash and dry pads. More function means more tanks to clean. Pick the least dock you will actually maintain. A neglected wash tray is the single most common reason owners complain of a bad smell.

The Q-series uses a JawScrapers comb and the Qrevo line uses a dual zero-tangle system. Both aim at hair. A pet household should check the roller every week regardless. Hair that is longer than about a hand span is the case that defeats any design sooner or later.

specDecoder.meaning: The brand name for its suction system. The Pa figure beside it is a peak motor rating.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Qrevo S5V lists 12,000 Pa and the Edge 3 Pro lists 36,000 Pa.

specDecoder.meaning: An arm that extends the side brush or mop toward corners and baseboards. It improves edge coverage.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Qrevo 2 Pro and Qrevo S5V both carry it.

specDecoder.meaning: A laser distance sensor that drops into the body when not needed. It lowers the height without losing the map.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Edge 3 Pro uses it to stay at 3.46 in.

specDecoder.meaning: The brand's 3D sensing system for mapping and obstacle avoidance. It sees shape and height.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Saros 10R uses it, and the listing implies more than a laser.

specDecoder.meaning: The maker estimate for the dock bag. Hair and dust load shorten it.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Q-series bag dock quotes 7 to 9 weeks from 2.7 L.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mop reach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared FlexiArm models with fixed-pad models. The Qrevo 2 Pro and S5V lead on edge coverage. Robots without an extending mop were marked down for baseboards.

howWeEvaluated.title: Body and climbing
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared heights such as 3.14 in on the Saros 10R and 3.46 in on the Edge 3 Pro, plus listed threshold climbing. Clearance and climb decide where a robot can work. Models that fit both scored highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dock design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared charge-only, bag and wash docks. The Qrevo line adds drying, and the Q-series stays simple. Convenience was weighed against tanks to clean. A dock with no drying stage was marked down in humid climates.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensing and privacy
howWeEvaluated.description: We read listings for laser, 3D sensing and object recognition. Laser-only robots keep exposure low, and the Edge 3 Pro and Saros 10R add sensing that implies a camera. Buyers decide the trade.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed repeated owner reports on dock leaks, app issues and brush wear. Patterns outweighed single complaints. Spare-part supply across the range counted in the brand's favour.

cards.label: Laser only
cards.text: The Q7 L5 and bag-dock Q-series map by laser and name no objects. They keep lens exposure low.

cards.label: Recognition
cards.text: The Edge 3 Pro and Saros 10R sense and name obstacles. They avoid cords better but imply camera-style sensing.

howToChoose.note: Pick laser-only for privacy and recognition for cluttered floors. Neither choice changes the dock, which is a separate decision.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A zero-tangle or comb brush, a dock that handles bulky hair and edge reach for pet beds along walls. Obstacle recognition helps with pet accidents.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Qrevo 2 Pro adds dual zero-tangle brushes and FlexiArm. The Edge 3 Pro adds recognition for accidents.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have thresholds, low furniture or cluttered floors. The Edge 3 Pro and Saros 10R solve those.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have flat hard floors. The Q7 L5 or the bag-dock Q-series is enough.

maintenance.task: Wipe the laser or sensor window
maintenance.why: Dust blurs the sensor and causes drift. Use a dry cloth. Check the flexible arm and side brush joints for trapped grit whenever you wipe the tray, because a stiff arm will stop extending without any error message.
Grey water sours quickly. Leave the lid open to dry.
Even zero-tangle designs keep strands at the end caps. Cut them along the groove.
The Q-series bag is quoted for that range. Replace sooner with pets.
Hard water scales pumps and the FlexiArm spray. Run descaler through the clean tank. Skipping this step is the most common cause of weak water flow on mop docks.

faq.q: Which Roborock is best for pet hair?
faq.a: The Qrevo 2 Pro has a dual zero-tangle system and a wash dock. The Q-series with a JawScrapers comb is cheaper and also sheds hair. Check the brush weekly with either.
No. The number is a peak rating. Edge reach, brush design and thresholds matter more in daily use.
The Q-series uses laser mapping, and the Edge 3 Pro and Saros 10R add recognition or 3D sensing that implies more. Check the maker page for the model you pick.

faq.q: Is the Q7 L5 enough for a house?
faq.a: It maps well and runs by laser, but it has no dock and the lowest suction here. Large houses benefit from a dock. Flats are fine.

faq.q: How long do the bags last?
faq.a: The Q-series bag is quoted at 7 to 9 weeks from 2.7 L. Pet hair shortens it. Check at one month.
The Edge 3 Pro is listed as gliding over thresholds, and the others rely on standard climbing. Measure your doorway tracks before choosing.
